fullPassage: [Analysis] It takes on average half a second for the unconscious mind to process incoming sensory stimuli into conscious perceptions. Yet we are not aware of this time delay — you think you see things move as they move, and when you stub your toe you get the impression of knowing about it right away. This illusion of immediacy is created by an ingenious mechanism, which backdates conscious perceptions to the time when the stimulus first entered the brain. On the face of it, this seems impossible because cortical signals take the same "real" time to process to consciousness, but somehow we are tricked into thinking we feel things earlier. One way it might be explained is that consciousness consists of many parallel streams and that the brain jumps from one to another, revising them and redrafting them. [1] We not only absorb our moral codes and definitions of right and wrong from the group; the group also transmits cues about cooperation and defection and what it means to act in a trustworthy manner. People are more likely to suppress their self-interest in favor of the group interest if they feel that others are doing so as well, and they're less likely to do so if they feel that others are taking advantage of them. The psychological mechanism for this is unclear, but certainly it is related to our innate sense of fairness. We generally don't mind sacrificing for the group, as long as we're all sacrificing equally. But if we feel like we're being taken advantage of by others who are defecting, we're more likely to defect as well. [2] In their pre-predatory stage, our primate ancestors had moved through the world among other creatures that did not fear them. Once they adopted carnivory, the prey they were interested in learned to allow close approaches at their own risk. But unlike big cats or terrifying wolves that were obvious predators, upright primates didn't automatically fit the predator template for most animals. Numerous examples from around the world during the past five centuries testify that upon initially encountering humans, many wild creatures did not associate us with a threat. In their first encounters with humans, scores of species reacted with trust and tameness. There is a term of art for this: biological first contact. When we appeared in new geographies for the first time, wild animals had to learn to be afraid of us. Many died standing and looking, never absorbing the lesson. [3] Consider the following two everyday linguistic expressions: "The election is ahead of us" and "the long Winter is now behind us." Literally, these expressions do not make any sense. "An election" is not something that can physically be "ahead" of us in any measurable or observable way, and the "Winter" is not something that can be physically "behind" us. Hundreds of thousands of these expressions, whose meaning is not literal but metaphorical, can be observed in human everyday language: "he is a cold person," "she has strong opinions," "the market is quite depressed." Metaphor, in this sense, is not just a figure of speech, or an exceptional communicational tool in the hands of poets and artists. It is an ordinary mechanism of thought. Usually operating unconsciously and effortlessly, it permeates nearly every aspect of human everyday (and technical) language, making imagination possible.

✅ ③ demonstrate: 증명하다/보여주다 — testify와 가장 가까운 동의어. 수많은 사례가 입증한다는 맥락 ←정답
❌ ④ adopt: 채택하다 — 증명과 무관
det.tip: testify ≈ demonstrate: 둘 다 '증명하다/입증하다'. 사례들이 사실을 입증한다는 문맥

questions.passage: Consider the following two everyday <u>linguistic</u> expressions: "The election is ahead of us" and "the long Winter is now behind us." Literally, these expressions do not make any sense. "An election" is not something that can physically be "ahead" of us in any measurable or observable way, and the "Winter" is not something that can be physically "behind" us. Hundreds of thousands of these expressions, whose meaning is not literal but metaphorical, can be observed in human everyday language: "he is a cold person," "she has strong opinions," "the market is quite depressed." Metaphor, in this sense, is not just a figure of speech, or an exceptional communicational tool in the hands of poets and artists. It is an ordinary mechanism of thought. Usually operating unconsciously and effortlessly, it permeates nearly every aspect of human everyday (and technical) language, making imagination possible.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 linguistic의 의미와 가장 가까운 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① verbal: 언어의/말의 — linguistic(언어적인)과 가장 가까운 동의어 ←정답
❌ ② physical: 물리적인 — 언어적이라는 의미와 무관
❌ ③ metaphorical: 은유적인 — 언어적 표현 중 은유적인 것은 하위 범주이지 동의어가 아님
❌ ④ measurable: 측정 가능한 — 언어와 무관한 의미
det.tip: linguistic ≈ verbal: 둘 다 '언어의/말의'. everyday linguistic expressions = 일상적인 언어 표현

questions.passage: It takes on average half a second for the unconscious mind to process incoming sensory stimuli into conscious perceptions. Yet we are not aware of this time delay — you think you see things move as they move, and when you stub your toe you get the impression of knowing about it right away. This illusion of immediacy is created by an <u>ingenious</u> mechanism, which backdates conscious perceptions to the time when the stimulus first entered the brain. On the face of it, this seems impossible because cortical signals take the same "real" time to process to consciousness, but somehow we are tricked into thinking we feel things earlier. One way it might be explained is that consciousness consists of many parallel streams and that the brain jumps from one to another, revising them and redrafting them.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ingenious와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① brilliant: 뛰어난 — ingenious의 유의어
❌ ② creative: 창의적인 — ingenious의 유의어
❌ ③ clever: 영리한 — ingenious의 유의어
✅ ④ crude: 조잡한/투박한 — ingenious(기발한/정교한)의 반의어. 정교한 메커니즘의 반대는 조잡한 것 ←정답
det.tip: ingenious(기발한/정교한) ↔ crude(조잡한/투박한). 정교함과 조잡함의 대비

questions.passage: In their pre-predatory stage, our primate ancestors had moved through the world among other creatures that did not fear them. Once they adopted carnivory, the prey they were interested in learned to allow close approaches at their own risk. But unlike big cats or terrifying wolves that were <u>obvious</u> predators, upright primates didn't automatically fit the predator template for most animals. Numerous examples from around the world during the past five centuries testify that upon initially encountering humans, many wild creatures did not associate us with a threat. In their first encounters with humans, scores of species reacted with trust and tameness. There is a term of art for this: biological first contact. When we appeared in new geographies for the first time, wild animals had to learn to be afraid of us. Many died standing and looking, never absorbing the lesson.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 obvious와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① apparent: 명백한 — obvious의 유의어
✅ ② subtle: 미묘한/알아차리기 어려운 — obvious(명백한)의 반의어. 큰 고양이와 늑대는 obvious(명백한) 포식자지만 영장류는 subtle(미묘한) 위협 ←정답
❌ ③ evident: 분명한 — obvious의 유의어
❌ ④ visible: 눈에 보이는 — obvious와 유사한 의미
det.tip: obvious(명백한) ↔ subtle(미묘한). 늑대는 명백한 포식자, 영장류는 미묘하여 포식자로 인식되지 않았음

questions.passage:
(A) We not only absorb our moral codes and definitions of right and wrong from the group; the group also transmits cues about cooperation and <u>defection</u> and what it means to act in a trustworthy manner.
(B) The athlete's sudden <u>defection</u> from the national team shocked the entire sports community, as he chose to represent another country.
questions.stem: 다음 (A), (B)에서 밑줄 친 defection의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: defection: (A) 집단 이탈/배신 (협력을 거부하고 자기 이익 추구) / (B) 이탈/탈퇴 (소속 조직을 버리고 다른 곳으로 감)
det.analysis:
❌ ① (A) 결함 — (B) 탈퇴: (A)의 defection은 결함(defect)이 아닌 이탈/배신의 의미
❌ ② (A) 이탈 — (B) 결함: (B)의 defection은 결함이 아닌 탈퇴의 의미
✅ ③ (A) 배신/비협조 — (B) 이탈/전향: (A)는 집단 협력에서의 배신, (B)는 조직에서의 이탈/전향으로 각각의 문맥에 정확히 부합 ←정답
❌ ④ (A) 방어 — (B) 이탈: (A)의 defection은 방어(defense)와 무관
det.tip: defection: ① (사회심리) 집단 협력에서의 배신/비협조 ② (정치/스포츠) 소속 조직 이탈/전향

questions.stem:
다음 영어 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"to hold back or restrain something, especially one's own feelings or desires, in order to prevent them from being expressed or acted upon"

det.korean: 자신의 감정이나 욕구가 표출되거나 행동으로 옮겨지는 것을 막기 위해 억제하다 = suppress
det.analysis:
❌ ① transmit: 전달하다 — 억제와 반대 방향의 행위
❌ ② absorb: 흡수하다 — 받아들이는 행위이지 억제가 아님
❌ ③ sacrifice: 희생하다 — 무언가를 포기하는 것이지 억누르는 것은 아님
✅ ④ suppress: 억제하다/억누르다 — 감정이나 욕구를 표출되지 않도록 막는다는 영영 정의에 정확히 부합 ←정답
det.tip: suppress = hold back/restrain. 본문에서 suppress their self-interest(자기 이익을 억제하다)로 사용

questions.passage: Hundreds of thousands of these expressions, whose meaning is not literal but metaphorical, can be observed in human everyday language. Metaphor is an ordinary mechanism of thought. Usually operating _____ and effortlessly, it permeates nearly every aspect of human everyday language.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 주어진 단어를 문맥에 맞게 변형하여 영어로 쓰시오. (conscious)

det.analysis: 은유는 보통 '무의식적으로(unconsciously)' 그리고 힘들이지 않고(effortlessly) 작동한다. operating 뒤에 부사가 필요하고, and effortlessly와 병렬이므로 -ly 부사형이 와야 함. conscious → unconsciously (부정 접두사 un- + 부사 접미사 -ly)
det.tip: conscious(의식적인) → unconsciously(무의식적으로). 형용사 → un- + 부사 -ly 변환

questions.passage: It takes on average half a second for the unconscious mind to process incoming sensory stimuli into conscious _____. Yet we are not aware of this time delay.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 주어진 단어를 문맥에 맞게 변형하여 영어로 쓰시오. (perceive)

det.analysis: 감각 자극을 의식적 '인식들(perceptions)'로 처리한다. process A into B 구조에서 B자리에 명사가 필요. conscious(형용사)가 앞에 오므로 뒤에 명사가 와야 함. stimuli(복수)를 처리하는 결과이므로 복수형 perceptions가 적절.
det.tip: perceive(동사: 인식하다) → perception(명사: 인식) → perceptions(복수: 인식들)

questions.passage: In their pre-predatory stage, our primate ancestors had moved through the world among other creatures that did not fear them. Once they adopted carnivory, the prey they were interested in learned to allow close approaches at their own risk. But unlike big cats or terrifying wolves that were obvious predators, upright primates didn't automatically fit the predator template for most animals. Numerous examples from around the world during the past five centuries testify that upon initially encountering humans, many wild creatures did not associate us with a threat. In their first encounters with humans, scores of species reacted with trust and tameness. There is a term of art for this: biological first contact. When we appeared in new geographies for the first time, __________. Many died standing and looking, never absorbing the lesson.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 새로운 지역에 처음 나타났을 때, 야생 동물들은 '우리를 두려워하는 것을 배워야 했다'
det.analysis:
✅ ① wild animals had to learn to be afraid of us: 원문 일치. 처음 등장한 인간을 야생 동물이 두려워하는 법을 배워야 했다 ←정답
❌ ② many wild creatures associated us with a threat: '위협과 연관시켰다'는 앞 문장에서 이미 '연관시키지 않았다'고 했으므로 시간대 혼동
❌ ③ scores of species reacted with aggression: '공격성으로 반응했다'는 trust and tameness로 반응했다는 앞 내용과 모순
❌ ④ our primate ancestors adopted carnivory: '육식을 채택했다'는 이미 앞에서 언급된 과거 사건으로 빈칸 문맥과 불일치
det.tip: wild animals had to learn to be afraid of us = 야생 동물들은 우리를 무서워하는 것을 배워야 했다. 뒤의 'Many died never absorbing the lesson'과 직접 연결

questions.passage: We not only absorb our moral codes and definitions of right and wrong from the group; the group also transmits cues about cooperation and defection and what it means to act in a trustworthy manner. People are more likely to suppress their self-interest in favor of the group interest if they feel that others are doing so as well, and they're less likely to do so if they feel that others are taking advantage of them. The psychological mechanism for this is unclear, but certainly it is related to our innate sense of fairness. We generally don't mind sacrificing for the group, __________. But if we feel like we're being taken advantage of by others who are defecting, we're more likely to defect as well.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 집단을 위한 희생을 꺼리지 않는 조건: '모두가 동등하게 희생하는 한'
det.analysis:
❌ ① if we feel that others are defecting: '다른 사람들이 이탈한다고 느끼면'은 뒤 문장(But if...)과 내용이 겹침
❌ ② because the group transmits moral codes: '집단이 도덕 규범을 전달하기 때문에'는 앞 문장 내용의 반복이며 조건절 역할 불가
✅ ③ as long as we're all sacrificing equally: 원문 일치. 모두가 동등하게 희생하는 한 집단 희생을 꺼리지 않는다는 조건절 ←정답
❌ ④ when we suppress our self-interest: '자기 이익을 억제할 때'는 희생의 결과이지 조건이 아님
det.tip: as long as we're all sacrificing equally = 모두가 동등하게 희생하는 한. 공정성(fairness)의 핵심 조건

ch: if we feel that others are defecting
because the group transmits moral codes
as long as we're all sacrificing equally
